question.problem: Given that $w(x,y,z)=x{z}^{4}+y,$ find $\frac{∂w}{∂r},$ where $(x,y,z)$ are Cartesian coordinates and $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the corresponding cylindrical polar coordinates.
question.worked_solution:
Applying the multivariable chain rule for the function $w(x,y,z)$ with three independent variables $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ where $x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and $z=z,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r} & =\frac{∂w}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂r}+\frac{∂w}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂r}+\frac{∂w}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂r} \\  & =\frac{∂w}{∂x}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\frac{∂w}{∂y}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $w$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂x}={z}^{4},\,\frac{∂w}{∂y}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $r,\theta ,$ and $z,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂x} & ={z}^{4}, \\ \frac{∂w}{∂y} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r} & =({z}^{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +(1)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & ={z}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
